purpose: The participant row the Computer publishes into a call. Both the Python reference (shared/room_call_session.py) and the Swift model must agree, because this row is what tells participants what the Computer can and cannot do - and a client that renders it wrongly misrepresents the product's central claim.
notes: capabilities is exactly ['chat']. Anything else would mean the Computer had media authority, which the whole design exists to avoid.
hears_audio is false: it receives a transcript, not a track.
The notice is user-facing copy and is shown verbatim; it must never be rewritten per client.

listening.notice: Follows the conversation and replies in chat. It has no voice in the call and keeps no recording.

not_listening.notice: Follows the conversation and replies in chat. It has no voice in the call and keeps no recording.
